parsed.analysis: The reviewer is describing a login streak mechanic. They claim they played the previous night, yet the game reported that the streak was broken and reset their progress, wiping out roughly half of whatever the streak had accumulated. This is the classic daily-login incentive structure: the game rewards sustained daily returns and penalizes a missed day by breaking the streak and resetting the accumulated reward chain. Even though the reviewer attributes the reset to a faulty detection ('said I broke my streak and though I did not'), the underlying game rule itself imposes the streak-reset penalty, so the design pattern is present regardless of what triggered it.

labels.label: T_DailyRewards
labels.span: said I broke my streak and though I did not, it sent me right back to the beginning? sad, I was just playing last night...now today half of it is just gone?
labels.rationale: A streak that resets on a missed day and takes the accumulated progress with it is a daily login incentive with a penalty attached; the bug attribution applies only to the detection, not to the deliberate streak-reset rule, so the label holds under R11.

parsed.analysis: The reviewer describes network/performance failures inside PvP modes (Event and Duel): the game sticks or lags, controls stop responding, the session ends abruptly with a 'YOU HAVE LOST' verdict, and 30-50 ranked points are deducted. The reviewer blames the game-side connection (golden network icons) while insisting their own signal is fine, and asks for a fix. Under R11, a technical-fault attribution does not suppress a dark-pattern label where the underlying game rule itself imposes the penalty: the ranked match is a session that, once interrupted, costs the player rank progress regardless of why the interruption happened. That forfeit is the game's exit/session rule, only triggered here by the malfunction. No other game mechanics are described in the text.

labels.label: T_MandatoryMarathon
labels.span: game has suddenly stopped and says YOU HAVE LOST and then nearly -30 to -50 gaming points are lessed from my Ranked game progress
labels.rationale: A frozen/disconnected match still resolves to a loss and deducts ranked points, so the forfeit of progress follows the game's own session rule (matches cannot end for the player without losing rank progress) and is not merely the fault itself.

{
  "analysis": "The review is a largely incoherent compliment-and-complaint text. The only praise is for graphics. The complaint portion says the game has a listed/apparent size of 1GB, yet the reviewer's phone storage became full from this game, despite the phone (Red Magic 11 Pro) being capable of handling 30GB games. The final clause about \"pictures of fake\" appears to refer to store screenshots or listing imagery rather than in-game mechanics. parsed.analysis: The review describes Solitaire Grand Harvest's level-entry economy. Playing each level consumes credits, and the per-level cost has risen (2.8k per level) faster than the credits the player can earn from crops. Once credits run out, the only ways to keep playing are to wait an hour for the resource to come back or to pay cash for credits. So the review describes an energy-like resource that gates play on a real-time timer, with a paid shortcut that removes the wait.

parsed.analysis: The reviewer describes losing a seven-day login streak three times, despite not missing days. A login streak is a daily-return incentive: the game rewards consecutive daily logins and resets that accumulated progress when a day is missed. The reviewer attributes the loss to an unexplained fault, but the underlying design rule is that the streak is fragile and is lost, imposing the penalty on the player. Per R11, a bug attribution does not suppress the label where the game's own rule—streak reset—caused the forfeit.

labels.rationale: A login streak that is lost when a day is missed is a daily incentive with a penalty attached; the reviewer describes the streak resetting through no action of their own, which the game's streak rule enforces.
